scope: Proposition 11.3 (Quadratic transfer) of the manuscript “The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis: A Zero-Free Half-Plane $`\Re s\gt 7/8`$” (preprints/The-Quasi-Riemann-Hypothesis-September-30-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 003 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8fe93046f8cf5ef1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 84. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let σ0 ∈ [1/2, 1). Suppose every primitive finite-order Hecke L-function over F = Q( √ −3) is zero-free on ℜs > σ0, with its principal pole at one allowed. Then every finite-order Hecke L-function over F and every Dirichlet L-function is zero-free on that same strict half-plane, again allowing the principal pole at one.
